{{short description|Convergence of random variables in Banach spaces}}
The '''Itô–Nisio theorem''' is a theorem from [[probability theory]] that characterizes [[Convergence of random variables|convergence]] in [[Banach spaces]]. The theorem shows the equivalence of the different types of convergence for sums of independent and symmetric random variables in Banach spaces. The Itô–Nisio theorem leads to a generalization of Wiener's construction of the Brownian motion.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Nobuyuki|last1=Ikeda|first2=Setsuo|last2=Taniguchi|date=2010|doi=10.1016/j.spa.2010.01.009|issue=5|pages=605–621|journal=Stochastic Processes and Their Applications|title=The Itô–Nisio theorem, quadratic Wiener functionals, and 1-solitons|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304414910000189|volume=120|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> The symmetry of the [[Probability distribution|distribution]] in the theorem is needed in infinite spaces.

The theorem was proven by Japanese mathematicians [[Kiyoshi Itô]] and {{ill|Makiko Nisio|qid=Q102427262|short=yes}} in 1968.<ref name = "ItoNisio">{{cite journal |first1=Kiyoshi|last1=Itô|first2=Makiko|last2=Nisio |publisher=Osaka University and Osaka Metropolitan University, Departments of Mathematics |title=On the convergence of sums of independent Banach space valued random variables |journal=Osaka Journal of Mathematics |volume=5 |number=1 |date=1968 |pages=35–48 |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/osaka-journal-of-mathematics/volume-5/issue-1/On-the-convergence-of-sums-of-independent-Banach-space-valued/ojm/1200692040.full?tab=ArticleLink}}</ref>

== Statement ==
Let <math>(E,\|\cdot\|)</math> be a real [[separable space|separable]] Banach space with the norm induced topology, we use the [[Borel σ-algebra]] and denote the [[dual space]] as <math>E^*</math>. Let <math>\langle z,S\rangle:={}_{E^*}\langle z,S\rangle_E</math> be the [[dual pair|dual pairing]] and <math>i</math> is the [[imaginary unit]]. Let
*<math>X_1, X_2, \ldots</math> be an infinite sequence of independent and symmetric <math>E</math>-valued random variables defined on the same probability space,
*<math>S_n=\sum_{k=1}^n X_k</math>,
*<math>\mu_n</math> be the [[probability measure]] of <math>S_n</math>,
*<math>S</math> some <math>E</math>-valued random variable.
The following are equivalent:<ref name="ItoNisio"/>{{rp|40}}
# <math>S_n\to S</math> almost surely.
# <math>S_n\to S</math> in probability.
# <math>\mu_n \to \mu</math> in the [[Lévy–Prokhorov metric]].
# <math>\{\mu_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}</math> is [[Tightness of measures|uniformly tight]].
# <math>\langle z, S_n\rangle\to \langle z, S\rangle</math> in probability for every <math>z\in E^*</math>.
# There exists a probability measure <math>\mu</math> on <math>E</math> such that for every <math>z\in E^*</math>
::<math>\mathbb{E}[e^{i\langle z,S_n\rangle}]\to \int_{E}e^{i\langle z,x\rangle} \, \mu(\mathrm{d}x).</math>

'''Remarks:'''
Since <math>E</math> is separable, item&nbsp;3 (i.e. convergence in the Lévy–Prokhorov metric) is the same as convergence in distribution <math>\mu_n\implies \mu</math>. If we remove the symmetric-distribution condition:
* in a finite-dimensional setting equivalence is true for all except item&nbsp;4 (i.e. the uniform tighness of <math>\{\mu_n\}_{n \in \mathbb{N}}</math>),<ref name="ItoNisio" />
* in an infinite-dimensional setting <math>1\iff 2 \iff 3</math> is true but <math>6\implies 3</math> does not always hold.<ref name="ItoNisio" />{{rp|37}}
